extracted.intended_audience: European Union citizens, residents in a Member State, and companies/organisations/associations with headquarters in the EU who wish to submit a petition to the European Parliament
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on who may submit petitions to the European Parliament, what subjects and forms are acceptable, and how petitions are handled (Committee on Petitions). Intended to inform potential petitioners about eligibility, scope, and purpose of petitions under Article 227 TFEU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of petition (Article 227 TFEU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any citizen, acting individually or jointly with others, may at any time exercise their right of petition to the European Parliament under Article 227 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page frames petitioning as one of the fundamental rights of European citizens guaranteed by the Treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — EU citizens and residents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any citizen of the European Union, or resident in a Member State, may, individually or in association with others, submit a petition to the European Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural persons who are EU citizens or residents of a Member State may petition either alone or jointly with others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Companies, organisations and associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any company, organisation or association with its headquarters in the European Union may also exercise this right of petition, which is guaranteed by the Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal entities headquartered in the EU are explicitly permitted to submit petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition may be submitted on a subject which comes within the European Union’s fields of activity and which affects the petitioner directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two limits are highlighted: the subject must fall within EU fields of activity, and it must directly affect the petitioner (direct interest/impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible forms and interests
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition may take the form of a complaint or a request and may relate to issues of public or private interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions are not restricted to public-interest matters; private-interest issues and both complaints and requests are acceptable forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content — application of EU law / appeal to adopt a position
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition may present an individual request, a complaint or observation concerning the application of EU law or an appeal to the European Parliament to adopt a position on a specific matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions that raise issues about how EU law is applied, or ask the Parliament to take a position, are explicitly within scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — drawing attention to infringements of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Such petitions give the European Parliament the opportunity of calling attention to any infringement of a European citizen’s rights by a Member State or local authorities or other institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One key objective of petitions is to alert the Parliament to alleged infringements of citizens' rights by Member States, local authorities or other institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling body — Committee on Petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee on Petitions is composed of 35 Members and is headed by a Chair and 4 Vice-Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions submitted to the Parliament are considered by the Committee on Petitions; the page names the committee and gives its basic composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission mechanism — Petitions Portal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page provides/points to an online Petitions Portal as the mechanism to start/submit a petition to the European Parliament.
